newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong coffee companies say price hikes brewing.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong coffee companies say price hikes brewing.

text.p: Coffee wholesalers and retailers in Hong Kong, dismayed by fresh rallies in prices, were considering putting up prices, coffee sources said on Friday.
"It's a very serious problem," said one wholesaler. "When the raw material is going up, what can you do? We are considering price hikes."

July delivery coffee at New York's Coffee Sugar and Cocoa Exchange closed 19.25 cents or six percent higher at US$3.15 per pound on Thursday after rising as high as US$3.18, the highest price for coffee on the exchange in two decades.
Consuming and producing countries' depleted inventories, hovering near 20-year lows, have been behind the sustained five-month run-up in coffee futures.

"We increased our price from HK$22 per pound to HK$24 per pound last month and are considering raising prices again," said an official at an import firm which sources most of its beans from Indonesia.
But intense competition in Hong Kong's coffee market made for a delicate game, with companies testing the market to see how high they could push prices, sources said.
"Old customers will be protected and new customers pay the new price," one supplier in the British colony said.

"Our prices have so far seen an eight percent increase. In Hong Kong there are so many competitors, so we have to see what the public can take and see the stock we have," another raw coffee bean importer said.
He said some big sellers have no stock but others were saying they had no stock while waiting to see where prices were heading.
People in Asia were drinking more coffee, even in China where tea has an ancient tradition, industry sources said.

Some coffee manufacturers in Hong Kong and China said earlier this month their prices would remain unaffected in the short term but that they would be forced to take measures if prices continued marching up.
